observations: Photo 0: front of a small black desktop tower UPS with a blue centre strip, one round power button and three indicator LEDs (AC, battery, fault symbols).
Photo 0: 'BLUE GATE' moulded on the front top; no model number or VA/watt rating visible.
Photo 0: LEDs appear off; no sign the unit is powered.
Photo 1: side and top view; input cable with a three-pin round plug lying on the top; vents on the side.
Photo 1: visible dust and specks on the top and scuffs on the front panel; used, not boxed.
Rating label, rear outlets and battery compartment are not shown.

read_from: photo 0 front, 'BLUE GATE' moulded above the blue strip

claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show a Blue Gate desktop UPS.
Photo 1 shows dust and specks on the top and photo 0 shows scuffs on the front; it is a used unit.
Internal history and battery replacement cannot be seen in photos.
LEDs are off in photo 0; no clip of it powering on or holding a load on battery.
No receipt or warranty card is shown.

risks.risk: Battery dead or weak, so the UPS gives no backup time.
risks.proof: Clip with a load plugged in (lamp or PC), then the wall supply unplugged, showing it keeps running for a minute.

risks.risk: Unit does not power on or has an inverter/charging fault.
risks.proof: Clip pressing the power button with the indicator LEDs lighting and the beep.

risks.risk: Capacity unknown; a smaller VA rating is worth less.
risks.proof: Photo of the rating label on the back or underside showing model and VA rating.
risks.if_unproven: As the smallest desktop capacity in the range.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged rear outlets or cables.
risks.proof: Photo of the back panel showing all output sockets.

proof_requests: Clip powering it on with a load plugged in, then pulling the wall plug to show it holds the load on battery.
Photo of the rating label showing model and VA rating.
Photo of the back panel and outlets.
Photo of the receipt and warranty card with a handwritten code in shot.
response.reason: The brand Blue Gate is readable and it is clearly a small desktop UPS, so it can be priced at its worst case: smallest capacity, battery dead and not proven working.
